passages.context: Whiston VIII.2.5 presents Josephus's claim that God gave Solomon skill against demons and Josephus's first-person report of seeing Eleazar perform before Vespasian and a military audience. The described means include a ring and root at the nostrils, mention of Solomon and recitation of attributed incantations, and a command that the departing demon overturn a water-filled cup or basin. The passage supports Josephus's literary testimony and framing, not the mechanism, Solomonic authorship, or continuity into Christian ritual.

work.author: Flavius Josephus
work.description: Josephus's twenty-book history of the Jewish people, completed c. 93/94 CE. Book 12 retells the Letter of Aristeas's account of the Greek translation of the Law under Ptolemy II. Loci use book with Whiston chapter or chapter.section numbering; consumers state which numbering they follow.
